newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela tax collection to reach 12 pct GDP by 99.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela tax collection to reach 12 pct GDP by 99.

text.p: Venezuelan tax collection is set to rise to 12 percent of Gross Domestic Product (GDP) by the end of the century, tax superintendency president Edgar Paredes Pisani said.
"It's definitely possible when you consider that taxes contributed 9.5 percent of GDP in 1996, a year of recession," Paredes Pisani told reporters.

Increased tax collection forms part of a long term strategy to balance Venezuela's fiscal dependence on oil revenues. Last year, state-owned oil company remitted $10 billion to the national treasury, equivalent to some 14 percent of Gross Domestic Product.
Tax collection targets for the year are 3.5 trillion bolivars ($7.3 billion), up from 3.2 trillion last year, Paredes Pisani said.
Tax collection for the first two months of the year is at 541 billion bolivars, 14 percent above tragets, he added, with sales taxes accounting for some 60 percent of that revenue.
